subject: Renewal & Upsize: reserved GPU add-on and surge handling options
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@cloudflix.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: cluster expansion & surge handling options

Hi Vanessa,

As we approach our Feb 1 renewal I wanted to surface CloudFlix's asks so we can lock terms quickly: we want to add 8 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs to the current pool (7x current commit -> total reserved 40 GPUs) and get a 99th percentile throughput target for our standard inference route (target: 250 tokens/sec sustained per pod for 2k token windows).

Big open question for us is burst: our traffic occasionally spikes (global sporting events). We prefer a mix of guaranteed reserved capacity + an on-demand overflow that can scale to an extra 16 GPUs, but wanted a billing guardrail so we don't face unexpected charges during a three-hour flash spike. Alternatively, we can agree on a hard cap (no overflow) and accept queued/delayed requests during spikes — but that may be unacceptable for some product flows.

Can you confirm pricing for the 8-GPU add-on, proposed SLA language for the throughput SLO, and options for a spend cap / alerting for burst spillover? Also, do you have a contract amendment we can start reviewing?

Thanks,
Amit
Amit Shah
Head of Platform Engineering
CloudFlix Inc.

Hi Amit — thanks for the clear summary. TL;DR: we can do the 8-GPU reserved add-on, confirm a 99th percentile throughput SLO (250 tokens/sec per pod for the configured 2k window) with penalty credits for sustained breaches, and offer two burst patterns:

1) Overflow-on-demand (preferred): up to +16 GPUs for spikes, billed at a higher on-demand rate; customers can set a monthly maximum spend cap and automated alerts at configurable thresholds (example: 50%, 80%, 95% of cap). If cap is hit, overflow is paused and traffic falls back to reserved-only routing.

2) Hard-cap (no overflow): traffic beyond reserved capacity is queued or sent through a lower-priority path with slower throughput — no additional billing but risk of increased latency / rejected requests.

I'll loop in Aditya (pricing) and Evelyn (SE) to confirm numbers and SLA wording. I'll attach a draft amendment (v3) for redlines.

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood provides price for 8-GPU add-on + example billing cap tiers by EOD Tues
- SE to validate throughput profile against their workload (Evelyn)
- Legal/contract amendment sent for review with DocuSign link

Will follow up with the pricing matrix.

Best,

Hi Amit,

I ran a quick sim against the sample traces in your spreadsheet (thanks) and two notes from an SE perspective:

1) Sustaining 250 tokens/sec per pod at 2k window is achievable on A100-equivalent profiles with the right batch sizing and KV cache hit rate > 60%. We'll need to tune request routing to prefer warmed pods for high priority traffic.

2) Overflow-on-demand works but you should plan for prefix caching and graceful degradation for non-critical endpoints. For the global sporting-event scenario I'd recommend: reserve the 8 GPUs + a small guaranteed buffer (8 GPUs warm standby in the reserved pool) and then an overflow budget (we can commit to a low-rate reserved burst: 64 GPU-hrs/month at reduced rate as Aditya suggested) to avoid surprise bills.

If you want, I can run a 48-hour load test on our staging cluster with your top 10 routes and produce a latency vs cost tradeoff matrix.

Cheers,
Evelyn Hart
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Amit Shah <amit@cloudflix.com>

Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 16:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: cluster expansion & surge handling options

Vanessa / Aditya / Evelyn — thanks all for the quick turnaround and concrete options. CloudFlix prefers option (1) overflow-on-demand with a monthly spend cap and the blended pre-commit for predictable burst (Aditya's blended model). Please proceed with:

- Amendment that adds 8 reserved GPUs (term: 12 months) at the net rate you proposed
- Add a burst program: 64 GPU-hrs/month at $65/GPU/hr + overflow-on-demand billed at $120/GPU/hr up to a monthly spend cap of $12,000; when the cap is reached overflow pauses and requests route to reserved-only or fall back path.
- SE-led 48-hour load test on staging the week of Jan 18.

Once we have the amendment I'll route to procurement for sign-off. Lenora is on copy to coordinate procurement and legal.

Best,
Amit
